cs.t: A Steam Deck is a bit more lumpy than the Minibook. I find it a lot easier to put my Minibook into a rucksack as it's thin, so it can just slide between stuff. The Steam Deck is quite a lot bigger, though I often take both on holiday as they fill different needs.
cs.th: Chuwi Minibook X: the netbook we deserve

cs.t: I love mine:  https://taoofmac.com/space/reviews/2025/05/15/2230  - I run Silverblue with niri and Noctalia Shell and it is very zippy, besides being able to drive huge external monitors.
cs.th: Chuwi Minibook X: the netbook we deserve

cs.t: Confirmed. Minibooks are amazing in cramped locations (for example, airplane seats), or just to always keep in the bag for support. There's nothing in the market like them, which is a shame - I think a slightly better quality Minibook (Chuwis are plain crap) would be a very solid laptop.
cs.th: Chuwi Minibook X: the netbook we deserve

cs.t: I loved my HP 200LX, and I bought a Planet Gemini as well as a GPD Pocket for the same reasons you described. But I am also 55, and my eyes can't deal any more with a screen less than 11" in a general-purpose computing device (as opposed to a phone or tablet, which have an OS and GUI designed for the small screens), so my portable devices are now a Chuwi Minibook X and a Thinkpad X13. The Thinkpad is a revelationm as despite its size it is lighter than almost anything else, including an iPad with a Bluetooth keyboard.
cs.th: The Typeframe PX-88 Portable Computing System

cs.t: It's a shame that tablets have made this kind of form factor less desirable (also Microsoft did hobble them by reducing Windows licenses for them and thus the machines became less capable than the Linux powered ones). I'm a big fan of UMPCs - there's something very useful about having a physical keyboard so you can do serious work when needed but don't want to carry around a large laptop. I've got a Chuwi Minibook (8inch screen) for that kind of usage and happily runs Linux on it nowadays (older versions of Ubuntu used to periodically hang which I believe was an issue with a driver for the disk).
